text:
She asked coyly. Her cheeks were flushed with both her pleasure and the slightly awkward embarrassment that filled her.
‘Ridiculous,’ Nicolas laughed, ‘listen to this…’
‘Do I have to?’
‘Yes, Madam, you do. I just made every effort to please you, now you have to listen to me. It’s called equity, Dr Riesigerschwanz told me all about it. He made it adamantly clear, if I please you, you are obliged to do as I say, that is how relationships work. I don’t know how we are supposed to get married when you don’t even know the basics.’
‘I’m not marrying you, Nic, I told you this. I don’t want to get married. Not to you. Not to Chester. Not to anyone. I have my own plans.’
‘IT SAYS,’ Nicolas bellowed to drown out Allyra’s protests, ‘as she lay in the afterglow, he placed his hands on her body and massaged her skin with the tenderness of a lover smitten. For hours he kneaded her shoulders and back…’ Nicolas snorted, ‘Yes, I can’t be bothered with all that. It seems a little one sided too. In fairness, if anyone should be massaging anyone, then it should be you massaging me for my astounding performance or at least giving me some money.’

Allyra’s jaw dropped in response to Nicolas’s magnanimous monologue,
‘That is a little insulting, Nic.’
Nicolas ignored her and parked his regal behind in his chair,
‘Aftercare, what absolute nonsense. I am a busy man, I don’t have to be a voluntary physiotherapist, no matter what strange woman ideas you have about it.’
‘I never mentioned it,’ Allyra sighed, ‘you brought all this up when, literally, no one asked!’
‘Next you will want jewellery and chocolates. I have seen you sniffing around the chocolate eclairs in the Sapari bakery, and flowers, you will want them too. I shall be inundated with bees. Then you will ask me to move furniture around only to have me move it all back the next day. You will probably want scented candles delivered daily. Then it will be, Nicolas would you love me if I was a slug? And all that entrapment, before you know it, Corax will be a Tupperware shop filled with free women who all hate me. No, this won’t do. I don’t think I should marry you at all, not with this attitude.’
‘Good, don’t,’ Allyra snapped.
Nicolas pursed his lips, twitched and snorted again,
‘Worry nor, fair maiden, for I shall overlook these failures that saturate my queen’s troubled heart.’

Allyra contemplated asking him again why he spoke in such a weird way, but guessed he would just misfire again or talk more gibberish, and she could not be bothered with either,
‘So, what happens now?’
‘Now? Past. Present and future, or just present?’
‘Any.’
Nicolas cleared his throat, which was a tad slimy,
‘A raven shall carry you yonder and a friend and a stranger shall seduce you as one does when one is one, then you shall drown in my oblivion, marry me as you promised, and lock yourself in a birdcage.’
Allyra waved her hand,
‘Never mind. May I leave?’
‘Indeed, I must prepare for our date tonight.’
‘Whatever you say, Nic.’
‘That’s the spirit,’ Nicolas grinned, ‘now you wish to go to the Sapari Tavern?’
‘I do.’
‘I will hear that again within three moons,’ Nicolas smirked.
‘I’m sure you hear it all the time.’
Nicolas’s mouth opened again, astonished by Allyra’s intuitive mind,
‘Madam, you are correct. Have you ever been told that you must be psychic?’

Allyra had given up talking and let Nicolas continue,
‘We must, unfortunately, delay your movement to enable our good self, the Pied Piper, to pork his way through the sands of Neferaten. I sense that matters are not going his way and it will take him longer than one usually takes to deliver the post!’
Allyra shook out her hands,
‘I am supposed to meet Chester after his shift.’
‘He’s running late,’ Nicolas snapped, ‘I just told you this.’
‘How would you know?’
Nicolas’s eyes shifted from side to side,
‘Would you do me a service, Immoless?’
‘What?’
‘I should like you to sit in my chair, just stand and I shall move, and then you sit.’
Allyra tutted,
‘I’m not a dog.’
Nicolas’s face dropped, and he made every effort to look hurt,
‘Please, humour me!’

Nicolas stood and allowed Allyra to sit, albeit uncomfortably and a little suspiciously, in his chair.
‘Excellent,’ Nicolas smiled, ‘it suits you, Immoless.’ He moved his face in front of hers. His eyes flashed bright green. Allyra’s eyes whitened in response.
‘Time, time, time.’ Nicolas murmured, ‘You can wait there quietly until Ches returns. When you wake you shall be convinced that you chose to stay and we had a very romantic dinner together.’ Nicolas clicked his fingers, and Allyra’s eyes closed completely.

Nicolas took out his pocket watch and watched as each second ticked by. Every clock in Sapari stopped. Every watch stopped and Nicolas remained still for hours.

Eventually Webster appeared in the glass of Nicolas’s pocket watch,
‘I am pleased to inform you that Chester’s day was most successful. Cedric, Ledgerly and Pauley have assisted. Chester has dined, changed, and is on his way to Sapari as I speak.’
‘Excellent,’ Nicolas said.

The clocks resumed their movements.

Nicolas clicked his finger in Allyra’s face,
‘Did you enjoy your dinner, Immoless?’ He asked.
‘Yes, thank you, I,’ Allyra hesitated, ‘actually no, I…’
Nicolas opted to ignore the glitch and interrupted,
‘Now, we must depart. I shall escort you to the tavern, and you shall reward me with a kiss, to show everyone who you belong to.’
‘I can escort my…’ Allyra’s protest was cut short.

Nicolas pulled her from the chair, dragged her to the window and dropped the two of them into a crouching position. Intestines spewed about Allyra, then a pulsating heart, followed by a liver and bone. Then came muscle, flesh and skin, and finally feathers smoothly formed around them. Instinctively Allyra clung to Nicolas,
‘What’s happening?’ She asked, her voice muffled by the raven’s body that smothered her.
‘I’m taking you where you wish to go.’

The raven that engulfed Allyra and Nicolas trotted about the floor, then took flight, darting through the window and shooting backwards into the sky as lightening kissed its bleak beak. The bird soared, circled Sapari an unnecessary amount of times, and landed outside of the tavern. The feathers retracted first, then the skin, flesh, bone and organs until Allyra was left on the quayside vomiting in Nicolas’s arms. Nicolas was extremely flattered by Allyra’s digestive offerings and held her close to him. He wiped her mouth with his sleeve, declared that he would never wash the love offerings from his suit or indeed ever wash his suit again, then stood her up. Allyra dizzied and fell, but Nicolas caught her,
‘Is that your first flight?’
Allyra nodded, then fell again enabling Nicolas to catch her again. This pleased Nicolas. He pushed his shoulders back, and spoke with a deeper voice,
‘You are saved, my queen.’
Allyra did not answer but talk of the scene quickly drifted through the sprawling gossip train taking the story of Nicolas and Allyra’s torrid love affair from the outside of the tavern to the inside of the tavern, and Banshee came out for a nose.

Nicolas grabbed Allyra and swung her backwards over his arm, lowered her body, and shoved his face into hers,
‘Alas, my queen, I must depart and prepare for tonight,’ Nicolas said as loudly as possible, then pulled Allyra up, grabbed both of her shoulders firmly and plunged his tongue deep into her throat, whilst allowing his lips to grind against hers. His body found itself grinding against her as well. Allyra did not find his lips as offensive as she initially thought, indeed, Nicolas was growing on her. Her own mouth responded to him. Nicolas then stepped back, bowed and sunk into the raven before departing.

Scene VIII: The Hobnailed Boot

The 2ndDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Sapari

Once the raven disappeared into the dusk, Banshee, who had been staring along with the other nosey parkers, scurried up to Allyra and placed an arm about her shoulder,
‘Honey, am I imagining things or was that…?’
‘Nicolas DeSilva,’ Allyra replied.
‘I didn’t know you knew each other, you never told me.’
Banshee brushed the hair from Allyra’s eyes and glared at the blood, ‘Did he hurt you?’
Allyra shook her head.
‘But the blood?’
‘It’s his blood. He vomited on me and I don’t really know him. He has just been following me around for two days.’
Banshee laughed,
‘You could have fooled me! I saw the white stain on his trousers. Looked fresh too. You nasty!’
Allyra shook her head and wiped the vomit from her clothes. The vomit did not want to depart as it had fallen in love with the blood, and the two started to mingle quite happily. Allyra looked Banshee in the eye,
‘I don’t know him. I don’t know him. I don’t know him. I don’t know him. He has been following me around all day.’

Banshee looked Allyra up and down,
‘Calm yourself, Lyra. You have a meeting with Lord Fuckwad soon, you can’t go like that. Jump in the sea, then we can have a look at your makeup.’
Allyra dropped her kleptobag from her back, and handed it to Banshee,
‘Good idea.’ She kicked off her boots, walked to the quayside edge and jumped into the harbour. The cool water raised her spirits, and she rolled underneath its embrace. For a moment, she fancied that she saw the green-locked monster of her dreams watching her, then he was gone. The salt licked her lips. She swam about for short while, then made her way to the steps and climbed back up onto the quayside.
‘That’s much better,’ Banshee smiled as Allyra forced her boots back onto her sodden feet, ‘come.’
They entered the tavern, bypassing Nedi and Chester who were playing poker, and went straight to the ladies’ room. Banshee handed Allyra her bag and watched as Allyra used paper towels and cosmetics to tidy up her face.
‘I suggest you go to the room an hour early, use a sheet to dry yourself and prepare.’ Banshee advised.
‘I need to see Ches first.’
Banshee nodded in agreement; she knew better than to intercede on Chester’s behalf regarding any matter. Once Allyra looked a little more reasonable, both ladies exited the washroom and moved through the growing crowd to the corner booth where Chester and Nedi sat.

Banshee sat next to her beloved Nedi, and Allyra slid in next to Chester. Chester immediately threw his arms about her and held her in a lovingly tight grip,
‘I hear Hector pulled you from the sea again, Lyra,’ he purred, kissing her head, ‘I do worry about you.’
‘I know you do, Ches, but you really don’t need to.’
‘I will always worry about you.’ The Cat said, brushing his face up against Allyra as he let out a deep guttural purr, ‘You’re the best thing that ever happened to me. I couldn’t bear to lose you.’
Allyra laughed and touched his nose,
‘You always say that.’
‘And I mean it.’

Allyra reached for the drink Chester had had specially prepared for her. It was a dark red and green wispy cocktail. Chester insisted on ordering all of her drinks and had them made exactly to her taste. He even added a special serum that Allyra did not need to know about. Allyra took a sip before speaking again,
‘I dunno Ches. It’s been five years and I still don’t know where you live.’
‘Oh. That.’ Chester said, rubbing his head against her shoulder, ‘I’m always here for you, Lyra, you know that.’
‘That’s not the point, is it? Do you know I received an offer of marriage today? And yesterday! I’m not getting any younger, even though I will probably be dead soon, so I might just decide to accept the proposal!’ Allyra joked, even though she did not find the matter funny. Chester cupped her face in his hands and a gigantic smile spread from cheek to cheek,
‘One day soon, I shall take you home and marry you. That’s a promise.’
‘Mmm hmm,’ Allyra nodded, ‘I will be dead soon, Ches.’

Before the conversation shifted from tetchy humour to awkwardness, two gentlemen joined them. One was tall and muscular with a reddish beard, flaxen hair and grey eyes, and the other was tanned with very dark hair and eyes to match.
‘John, Jaeli,’ Chester nodded.
Allyra turned to the muscular man,
‘Can I get you a drink, John?’ Then shifted her gaze to Jaeli, ‘Jaeli?’
‘We would never ask a lady to buy,’ both said in unison. The brothers were a permanent fixture at the tavern, a necessity since they owned the establishment.

Other than Charmaine, who was off sick, all of the bartenders were male as, in 1531 P.V. John and Jaeli’s barmaids kept taking it upon themselves to disappear. At first their staff turnover saw the absence of two barmaids a moon, but this escalated to two barmaids a week.

The locals, being conspiracy nuts, put about a rumour that John and Jaeli were killing them and selling their body parts to the medical department at the Sapari university. However, John and Jaeli took a holiday to Neferaten, and the disappearances continued in their absence. Shortly after, a second rumour gained momentum. One that accused the great Nicolas DeSilva of declaring the women insane and stealing them away to Corax for lunch. Not lunch as in a date, but for his lunch.

The rumour was started by one Snoddle Copperbowl, a stout man whose puffy, purple face, oversized nose, and balding head informed the world that he was quite the brandy drinker. Mr Copperbowl made the heinous claim that he had seen DeSilva ‘Loitering about the quayside’ on the night that two of the barmaids went missing. Nicolas could not decide whether to take Copperbowl to court for misinformation or disinformation. Ledgerly let it be known, via a series of leaks, that both these issues were an ongoing problem in the Deep, as was tickturdery. After much deliberation, Nicolas further decided that both words; disinformation and misinformation had no meaning at all, and Mr Copperbowl just happened to have a nasty accident with a set of secateurs which culminated in him cutting his own head clean off.

The rumours were never mentioned again, and John and Jaeli retained Charmaine, the last living barmaid, and thereafter decided only to hire unpleasant looking, male bartenders.

It had occurred to John and Jaeli that, of late, Charmaine was not looking her best anyway.

‘Shall I deal you in?’ Chester asked the brothers.
‘Do,’ John replied, ‘what are the stakes?’
‘A night with Allyra!’
‘Fuck off with that!’ Allyra snapped.
‘Joking,’ Chester smiled, ‘let’s start at one hundred ardents.’
Chester shuffled the cards, fanning them, flailing them, bouncing them, and generally showing off as much as possible, then dealt everyone a hand.
‘Raise,’ Allyra and Chester said unanimously.
Nedi pulled on his beard,
‘I’m out.’
‘Banshee?’ Chester asked.
‘Raise.’
‘Jaeli?’
‘Raise.’
‘John?’
‘I’m out.’

Chester twiddled his hair,
‘Five hundred ardents.’
Allyra side-eyed him,
‘Six hundred.’
Jaeli looked form Allyra to Chester,
‘Forget it. I’m…’
Before Jaeli could finish his sentence, Chester’s nose inhaled sharply and he noted a change in the air. He rose, forcing Allyra to step out of the booth, and wandered about the tavern sniffing.
‘That’s gross,’ Banshee mumbled.
‘It’s just Ches.’ Allyra said as she watched him approach two red heads. Allyra lowered her eyes. Chester spoke to the ladies for a few minutes, then the two women stood and followed The Cat up the stairs.

Allyra turned over Chester’s cards revealing a royal flush,
‘That cheating rat!’
‘I don’t know why you put up with it!’ Banshee snapped.
Allyra slapped her own royal flush on the table,
‘I mean the cards. The other business doesn’t bother me.’
John shook his head,
‘It should.’
Allyra swallowed her drink in one go,
‘It doesn’t. We have an arrangement. Speaking of which, John, can I have my room key?’
John reached into his fawn suit pocket, pulled out a key and chucked it to Allyra who failed to catch it and had to go crawling about the floor to retrieve it. Once the key was in hand, she stood triumphantly,
‘Enjoy your game!’ She smiled and headed up the stairs.
Banshee and Nedi looked at each other but said nothing.

The room assigned to Allyra was fairly small. Lord Fuckwad did not come for the room. He came for the Allyra experience, and she was experienced. It was the sort of experience that loosened men’s tongues, and at times, their wallets. There was a small bed, which was a little too close to the window. It held a heap of fresh sheets and blankets that were tightly tucked under the mattress. Jaeli and John had been taught by their grandma, May, how to make a bed as difficult to navigate as possible.

May insisted on a bottom sheet, an under sheet, a duvet, a heap of blankets and a quilt. Allyra chose a blanket, stripped off and dried herself. She could hear the ladies that Chester had commandeered moaning in the next room and making an unnecessarily loud and irritating amount of noise.

Dressing again seemed a little pointless as Lord Fuckwad preferred her out of her clothes, so Allyra climbed into the bed and waited, and waited, and waited, until sleep took her.

She was crudely awakened, almost immediately, by a clonk on the head. Then another. Her body jumped and her eyes opened. The curtains were drawn, but the silhouette standing in the darkness seemed much taller than Lord Fuckwad,
‘What happened?’ Allyra asked.
‘You’re late, that is what happened.’
Allyra instantly recognised the deep voice and pulled one of the curtains enough to shed light on the situation. Nicolas stood before her. The dark glasses and fake moustache had made quite the comeback, and his cane, the tool with which he had awakened her, shimmered in the dusk glow.
‘I’m not late. Nicolas, why are you here?’
‘I am not Nicolas,’ Nicolas replied as he loomed over her, ‘I am Lord Fuckwad, now you have to fuck me.’
‘You are Nicolas, I am not fucking you, and where is the real Lord Fuckwad?’
‘I am Lord Fuckwad, but, alas, my predecessor met with a lonely ram who was so melancholy that he removed his heart with a slice of cucumber.’
‘Go away Nicolas,’ Allyra sighed.

‘Would you like me to depart and never return?’ Nicolas asked.
‘That would be nice.’
Nicolas laughed,
‘You jest, Madam. Such an adorable sense of humour.’
‘Nicolas!’ Allyra snapped, ‘Where is Lord Fuckwad?’
Nicolas removed his hat and placed it over his chest,
‘There was an incident. A horrific incident. After the removal of Lord Fuckwad’s heart he grew hysterical and drowned himself in the bilge of your ship, Madam, the Sombre. Quite grotesque it was. Fear not, the rats were so sympathetic to his plight that what they did not eat they shared with the sharks.’
‘So, you killed him?’
Nicolas sucked in a double breath of air,
‘Me, Madam? I could not harm a fly.’
Allyra ignored the performance and took another path,
‘How did you know I would be here? Are you spying on me?’

Nicolas leaned further forward and pressed his hands into Allyra’s thighs,
‘I was not tracking you. The passionate cries from the next room summoned me, and I indulged as your Cat did. It was a sight, the four of us. Your gentleman has no morals, none at all. You should see what he does with…’
‘No thank you,’ Allyra snapped, ‘that’s quite enough of that. I don’t believe you anyway. You keep making up rubbish.’
‘No lie has left my mouth, and I am wounded by such an allegation. Poor Nicolas, broken hearted yet again by your callous words.’
‘You are tiring is what you are.’
‘Thank you,’ Nicolas replied, whilst squelching his hat back into his greasy hair. ‘When I am your Lord and Master, I shall be faithful and merciful.’
‘Will you now?’ Allyra sighed.
‘Probably not,’ Nicolas’s hands reached up to his hat as it tried to escape from his sweaty head, and belted it firmly into place, ‘we shall marry at the Dokeshi Carnival, both times.’
Allyra remembered that she was naked, and shuffled under the sheets,
‘I’m not interested, and you are just talking for the sake of talking.’

Nicolas stared at Allyra,
‘You are naked, aren’t you? Such a welcome indeed.’
Allyra nodded towards the pile of clothes that lay on the floor,
‘Can I have my clothes?’
‘You probably can since they are yours, but they are not yours really, are they?’
Allyra clenched her fists and growled through her teeth,
‘Nicolas give me my clothes.’
‘I would rather not.’
‘And why not?’
Nicolas clonked her on the head with his cane again,
‘One does not talk back to one’s Master.’
‘I think I will come to Corax and commit myself, then you can just eat me and all this will be over with.’
Nicolas licked his lips,
‘I will be eating part of you later tonight.’
A pillow hurtled through the air and smacked Nicolas between the eyes,
‘Vulgar man!’ Allyra barked.
‘I am not a man; I am a demonic-God. Or just a god, and you were the one spreading yourself around my visage not a few hours ago. Encouragement indeed.’
‘You’re a pain in the ass, Nic!’

Nicolas grabbed Allyra’s foot from under the covers and dragged both Allyra and the blankets into his body,
‘You compliment me so beautifully, such poetic words.’
Allyra stifled an exhausted yawn,
‘Why are you doing this to me?’
‘It is a common fact that a gentleman must court a lady before the nuptial contracts are signed. It is good etiquette.’
Allyra placed her hand on Nicolas’s cheek, and stroked his face,
‘I want you to listen to me, Nic. We are not a couple. We are not getting married. My job is to pretend to slay you, your job is to execute me, that is how it goes.’
‘I think I was right, you know? A burgundy wedding dress to go with your hair.’

‘NICOLAS!’ Allyra shouted, but she wasn’t getting through.
‘And perhaps I will take you for your fitting,’ Nicolas continued. He then pulled a notebook and pencil from his inside pocket and scribbled down his thoughts. Allyra waited until he had finished and his ridiculous notebook had been returned to its home before bothering to speak again,
‘Are you happy now? And will you leave so that I can get dressed? As is a matter of gentlemanly decency.’
‘I am very happy, my love,’ Nicolas said, and he was happy, ‘but alas I cannot leave as whilst you were sleeping, I accidentally nailed my feet to the floor.’
‘Your nonsense has lost me a day of reconnaissance,’ Allyra moaned.
‘You do not need to torture my vampires further; I shall impart any Immortalis information you want as now is the time. Your wish is my command.’
Allyra looked at her poor clothes crying in the corner,
‘I wish you to leave.’
‘I already said that my feet are nailed to the floor. I cannot move.’

Allyra pulled away from Nicolas and clambered up the bed, dragging the blankets with her for the sake of modesty. She pulled the curtain open a little further to allow more light in, then crawled back down the bed to Nicolas and peered over the edge. His feet were indeed nailed to the floor. The nails had been tapped through his boots in bulk, and there was a puddle of blood running about the wood below. Allyra tutted, climbed out of the bed, and got dressed, giving Nicolas a very pleasing eyeful. She then threw her kleptobag on her back and headed to the door.
‘Nicolas’s feet hurt,’ Nicolas muttered, ‘please help him.’
Allyra stopped short of reaching for the door handle, sighed, and returned to her monstrous nemesis,
‘Fine. I will help you, then you leave me alone.’
Nicolas did not answer. Allyra picked up the claw hammer that Nicolas had left conveniently close to his boot, knelt down, and started tugging the annoyed nails from his feet.

‘I was thinking,’ Nicolas continued as he watched his bride build a pile of iron, ‘we could honeymoon on Sihr, since you like it so much. I know Elyas well, he’s an atrocious narcissist so he will probably allow it. He likes Monopoly, but you can’t play. I can play because I submitted my resume. I could draw a resume up for you, and then you can play too. I get the boot of course, and Elyas must lose. None of us let him win. Not even Robert, although Robert cheats. Elyas says Robert is dense, and I happen to agree, what do you think?’

Allyra stopped momentarily and looked up at Nicolas as one boot was released from its bondage. Nicolas knelt down next to her, did not wait for a response, and resumed his speech,
‘His name isn’t Theaten, of course, it’s Robert.’
‘His name is Theaten, and you know it’s Theaten.’ Allyra replied.
‘You are mistaken. Of course, His mother thinks his name is Theaten too, but I know better. He says it’s not, but that’s exactly what a Robert would say. He forgot his name when he started hanging around Count Pompous and his slut. Are you a fan of Count Pompous? I doubt it, no one is really. Undeserved gifts were bestowed I am afraid. Sad times. When I bestow gifts upon you, they shall be deserved, but you won’t like them. Robert would have been better off with Anne. Anne and Pompous’s marriage is an abomination, and it only gives Count Pompous fuel for his unwarranted arrogance.’

Allyra continued to pull at the nails, and Nicolas made it as difficult as possible by fidgeting.
‘He lies about me, you know? He tells the most atrocious stories to my brother, then I am inundated with Robert’s hideous company. You will meet Robert before the wedding.

text:
Your entire post was built around a fake Rolling Stone cover. That's not my opinion. That's a verifiable fact.

You then switched from defending the fake cover to claiming Trump made $4 billion. Fine. Show the evidence. Show the pre-presidency net worth, the post-presidency net worth, and the methodology used to arrive at that figure.

Trump was already a billionaire before entering office. If there is clear evidence that he enriched himself by $4 billion through abuse of office, present it. After a decade of investigations, lawsuits, congressional inquiries, prosecutors, journalists, and political opponents searching for exactly that kind of evidence, you would think the case would be straightforward if it were as obvious as you claim.

Instead, you've spent the entire conversation avoiding the one claim that was actually proven false: the cover was fake.

You call me illiterate, yet you're arguing with a fact you never refuted and defending evidence that never existed.

The cover was fake yesterday. The cover is fake today. And no amount of name-calling changes that reality.

Good day. You're about as entertaining as playing hangman by myself.

The difference between us is that when I log off, I go enjoy my life. I enjoy my family, my community, my country, and the president I voted for. Meanwhile, you'll wake up tomorrow still angry, still chasing outrage, still attending rallies, still picking fights with strangers you'll never meet, and still mistaking cynicism for substance and believing somehow in this argument you had a leg to stand on.

The irony is that after all of this, you've offered no facts, no evidence, and no rebuttal to the point that started the conversation. Just insults, deflections, and outrage.

The cover was fake. That was true at the beginning of this conversation. It's true at the end of it. And tomorrow, while you're searching for a new argument, it'll still be true, and your fictitious four billion will be profits in someone else's bank account you just talk about while being angry that you suck.

AMD was the strongest name yesterday — up 5.45% while Nvidia fell, then up 2% at the open. Then Hunterbrook's short report hit, and the stock fell as much as 9.5% intraday to $480.00, then steadied near $490. The report is called 'AMD Has Its Own China Problem,' and it flips the story investors had been telling: that AMD was the winner of Nvidia's China crisis. On the numbers, AMD's China exposure is bigger — 22.4% of revenue billed to China and Hong Kong in fiscal 2025, against 9.1% for Nvidia — plus $4.28 billion to Singapore.

Hunterbrook alleges blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems kept receiving updated AMD firmware after it was placed on the U.S. Commerce Entity List in March 2025 — at least six newer versions, most recently October 19. It names three affiliates — Maginfra in China, Kaytus in Singapore, and Aivres in California — selling servers built on AMD chips with firmware up to 99.94% similar to IEIT's. It also flags a January 10, 2027 rule change that could extend restrictions to foreign companies at least half-owned by blacklisted entities, plus today's BIS rule requiring licenses for advanced chips shipped to Singapore and four other countries. AMD also depends on Chinese partner Tongfu for much of its assembly and packaging.

Here is the red pen. Hunterbrook's fund is short @AMD — the report says so — so read it as an interested party's case, not a verdict. No export-control violation has been confirmed, and Hunterbrook could not determine how IEIT obtained the firmware or whether licenses existed. AMD did not answer, or say whether it holds the required licenses — silence, not an admission. The January rule is prospective, and the BIS rule is the same one from November 18, not a new ban on AMD's Singapore business. Still, the tape has spoken: even after the drop, AMD is up 128.81% this year, with analysts at Strong Buy and an average target of $657.74. Allegations, not proof — but a short seller's allegations move markets.

text:
Immortalis Book 1, The Jester and The Immoless

Act II: The Jester and The Immoless

Scene I; Prelude, The Pied Piper and The Beavers

The 2ndDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Sapari

During the small hours, a messenger arrived in Sapari on horseback. The horse was somewhat foolish looking. It appeared to grin and had huge goofy teeth. The new harbour master, a young man named Billy Botwell who had been dispatched from Threnodyl after the strange disappearance of the old harbour master, tried not to stare. He considered staring rude but could not help glancing every now and then at the strange beast. He even smiled at the horse in a moment of awkwardness, and the horse grinned back, making him feel even more awkward.

The situation worsened when a raven swooped down, landed on the quayside next to the horse, spilled in a heap of guts and bones and a red-headed pied piper, Chester, stepped out from the debris.

Chester grew to his full height as the raven reassembled itself. Billy rubbed his eyes in disbelief, put the whole experience down to the Ashurrel leaf he was chewing, and spat it on the walkway.

‘That’s government property you’re soiling there!’ Chester pointed out with some force, squaring up to the poor little lad. The messenger riding the overfriendly horse, who was clad in purple and wore an eye patch, waved a hand at Chester,
‘Easy now, the lad is clearly new!’

The messenger smiled at the lad, the lad smiled back, and the messenger’s smile dropped,
‘Pick it up! Ya filthy landlubber!’
Billy dropped to his knees and scooped up the damp leaves, and not knowing what to do with them shoved them back into his mouth and gagged.

The messenger ignored the retching and got straight down to business. He informed the new harbour master that his name was Bigglesworth, Commodore Bigglesworth or Commodore Nicolas Bigglesworth, and stated that he had ridden through the night along the coast to relay an urgent message. Pirates were headed to Sapari. Not a single pirate ship, but several, a fleet in fact. An armada. The pirates, Nicolai-Bigglesworth claimed, were intending to steal wood from the shipyard.

Billy did not think to ask where the message had emanated from or who had ordered its forwarding as he was still uneasy about the whole grinning horse and raven splatter debacle.

Once the message had been relayed, and Bigglesworth’s first job of the day accomplished, Bigglesworth turned to Chester and explained his next job of the day,
‘The Immoless!’ He stated, without further explanation.
‘Neferaten,’ Chester replied.

Chester then crouched down and the bone, guts and feathers of the same raven that had disturbed Billy, split apart, engulfed Chester and flew away at a speed only animals dosed with vampire blood could manage. Billy watched with his mouth agape, annoying Bigglesworth,
‘Well, boy! Don’t just stand staring, get the message out.’
Billy nodded and acted immediately.

Bigglesworth made haste on Nicolas’s goofy vampiric horse, Zimba, along the quayside, bypassed the town and rode into the Dokeshi Carnival where he tethered the horse. He then summoned the guardians of Dokeshi, two demonic clown lovers, Scurra and Phylax to stand guard. Once the demons were in position, Bigglesworth crouched and allowed an albatross to absorb him and flew out to The Sombre.

The harbour master, who was a little disturbed by all the carry on, immediately sent word to the shipyard, and advised that they move the wood, via a caravan, to the village of Ashurrel that bordered Togaduine. This, Billy reasoned, was the only logical course of action as Ashurrel was far from port. He did not want the workers to enter Togaduine as, it was believed, a tyrant ruled the kingdom. A tyrant based in Corax Asylum. The labourers at the shipyard acted immediately.

Nonetheless, the new harbour master, being a bit of a jobsworth, decided to undertake every precaution. He declared that all ships should leave port and anchor together building an impenetrable wall on the horizon, whilst avoiding the local fishermen to prevent produce diminishment. It just so happened that the same harbour master had been gifted a cargo of anchors not a week before, from the brand ‘Ferromagnetic DeSilva,’ at least that is what the boxes said.

The ships formed their wall, and used the anchors to secure their positions, but it became apparent by late afternoon that there was no pirate armada, and the ships attempted to return to shore. However, somewhere there was a reversal of polarity in the magnetic anchors and the ships slammed together crunching the hulls, buckling the decks, and causing a huge mess in the ocean. The debris was formidable, and everyone forgot about the wood.

When Billy finally dispatched a caravan to retrieve the wood they found it quite gone. Everyone was disgruntled, but before any investigation got underway Billy met an untimely death after a three ton anchor fell on his oversized head from a crane winch. The new harbour master soon became the old harbour master, and a harbour master from Ashurrel was sent to replace him, which was a little odd as Ashurrel had no proximity to the ocean. It was also a little odd that the new harbour master sported green locks, had eight eyes and called himself, ‘Rachnoc.’ The dock workers did not know what to make of Nicolai-Rachnoc and his excess of eyes, and rumours soon flew about that he was a loony recently escaped from Corax Asylum. The rumours were started by a dock labourer named Samson. The rumours stopped when Samson’s intestines accidentally released themselves from his body and wrapped around the drum of a dodgy capstan.

The Lord of Sapari wrote to Tepes to complain about the entire matter, and Tepes wrote to Theaten. Theaten forwarded his concerns to Nicolas by raven, and said letter was dumped, along with a few body parts, into the drains at Ashurrel.

No one knew who was responsible for the Ferromagnetic anchors, but some recognised the horse. And there were rumours.

There were also rumours about Chester. Some claimed that the love god, whose reputation preceded him, was a legend. Others believed he was Nicolas, or a cad, or a monster, and others still considered him to be an opportunistic postman. All rumours were, in fact, partially correct.

Chester was an infamous demon, infamous in Irkalla, and infamous in Corax Asylum, who Nicolas called the ‘The Pied Piper’ on account of the amount of beaver that followed him desperately trying to blow his massive flute. Nicolas was often jealous of Chester’s success with the ladies and put it down to his unusual appearance and impeccable taste. Chester was, in fact, a special Nicolai. He was the embodiment of Nicolas’s libido, his Evro, a walking dick and balls with the gift of the gab, and the skillset to match.

During the snowy first moon of 1536 P.V., Chester had spent his time building up a following of sorts around Neferaten. He moved from village to village keeping the ladies of every occupation and class warm. He found that dressing as a postman opened doors, and legs, with very little explanation needed. His raven allowed him to move swiftly between villages and broaden his portfolio of conquests. He had intended to return to his ladies sooner, but Nicolas insisted that he spent the second and third moon with Allyra on account of Nicolas and the prolific scientist and strategist Nicolai-Webster developing the new plan, Plan BAT, Belua Alvearis Tyrannus.

This restriction on Chester’s movements caused a day of yowling, sulking and whining, but Nicolas flipped his two-headed coin for the job, and Chester lost. Chester considered Nicolas and Webster’s plans to be a waste of time as previous plans and procedures to alleviate the recurring problem troubling the Nicolai had failed.

Webster called the problem Alveus Vacuus Problemus or AVP for short.

Several plans had been executed over several centuries, and all failed with quite horrific consequences. Nicolas and Webster had really upped the ante during the previous five years, but their plans continued to backfire. Webster blamed Nicolas, and Nicolas blamed Webster. Chester did not care who blamed who, he cared that his balls were temporarily in a sling. Nonetheless, he did adhere to the new plan and spent two moons being the perfect boyfriend. Of course, he had been Allyra’s ‘perfect’ boyfriend for the past five years, but he diligently increased love-bombing and worrying Allyra with his fake sympathy, mesmerism and coercion to enhance that appearance for Nicolas’s sake.

You see, Dear Reader, part of the problem worrying the Nicolai was that they did not have a queen, and part of the solution, Nicolas decided, involved taking a bride, and he had idealistic notions of how this should play out. These notions stemmed largely from his prolific reading of Carmilla Fanu’s dark romance novels. Nicolas somehow convinced himself that he was the dark handsome prince, protecting women from his own wrath. You could say that he misinterpreted the ideas behind the novels as he was conflicted in the realistic conveyance of the tropes.

Nicolas understood that first he had to be the beast, and threatening, and then he had to also be the dark, morally grey, romantic hero redeemed by love. Unfortunately, Nicolas failed to realise that these novels were fiction, and that the heroes were not nearly as repulsive as he was. The repulsive beast came quite naturally to Nicolas, but the hero side not so much, and he had no interest in personal redemption of any sort. He also failed to correctly comprehend the order of the narrative functions. In practice, this meant that most of the time his would-be brides were dead by Nicolas the Monster’s hand before Nicolas the Prince rocked up to save them.

Nicolas also misunderstood the word ‘no’ and interpreted it as the ‘princess’ being coy or shy, so when the potential bride reacted to his advances with some hostility, the beast became extraordinarily perturbed, and as such most of his plans failed spectacularly.

Now, Dear Reader, I have digressed a little from the prelude, or prologue, you may view it either way. This prelude focuses on the sufferings of Chester not the stupid ideas of Nicolas, so let us return to that.

Nicolas was more than ready to descend upon Allyra, show her the beast and the prince, and generally make her life difficult until she fell in love with him. Since Nicolas had planned a busy day of annoying Allyra, or as Nicolas called it, ‘seducing the Immoless’ Chester was free to revisit the pussies of the ladies of Neferaten and secretly get Allyra back for hitting Nicolas with a metal rod.

Unfortunately for poor Chester, the ladies had moved on.

Chester was quite happy to cheat and roam locating new conquests, and equally happy to dump any woman on a whim, but he did not take well to being the recipient of the same treatment.

He blamed the loose virtues of the women, not the manipulative natures of the men, for these atrocities and reacted with the wrath of a creature forlorn and broken-hearted by such cruel rejections.

The 2ndDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Neferaten

Chester took a detour to Corax, after his stopgap at Sapari, to change into his postman’s uniform, then flew directly to Tiye where hordes of beaver awaited his return.

The beavers had arrived in Neferaten during the first moon of the year. They had followed Chester there, as beaver followed Chester everywhere, it was a burden he had to bear. The beaver remained in Tiye where they dropped logs and dug holes.

Chester had not gone to Tiye to meet the beavers. Nonetheless, he did lead them quickly to a watering hole by one of the bridges and blessed them by biting his own wrist and adding a few drops of blood to the water for the sake of their virility and fertility. That was what he claimed anyway.

Chester actually returned to Tiye to meet with the beautiful thesapien glassblower, Thalia. Thalia had fascinatingly bobbed, brown hair with thick streaks of ginger, which Chester approved of, and was able to examine in some detail as he spent most of his time with Thalia during the first moon, staring at the top of her head or watching himself fuck her in the glass. He liked the ginger in her hair as he liked women who reminded him of himself. Chester had spent the entire first week of the first moon with Thalia who demonstrated her prolific blowing skills on him. She also showed him the processes surrounding glass manufacturing.

Although Nicolas had only offered Chester a day to hump his way through Neferaten on this occasion, a challenge Chester was more than capable of meeting, he had hoped to see Thalia’s head one last time before ending their courtship.

Chester desperately wanted to surprise Thalia with his magnificent presence, and even considered railing her with his gloriously long tongue as a thank you. As such, our cat walked the circumference of the warehouse, climbed up the outer wall to the window and peered in.

Chester liked to spy and stare, it was a common trait among the Immortalis who framed it as reasonably protective and caring behaviour as opposed to downright creepy and wrong.

Thalia was busy blowing pipes, but there was no glass involved. Instead, she was blowing the pipes of the tanner and the cheesemaker, at the same time. It was one thing for Chester to romance three or four women at once, but for a woman to do it with multiple men seemed crude and outrageous. This, however, did not stop Chester staring, and one hand took a wander into his pants as the other paw clawed into the woodwork keeping him balanced.

Passers-by opted not to look up as rumour had it that the sadist Nicolas masqueraded as a postman or a pied piper, also the people of The Deep were also used to postmen slipping more than letters into the women’s boxes.

Once all loads had been blown, Chester decided to pay Thalia a visit to confront her about her infidelity, even though they were not in a relationship. He waited until both men made their hasty departure, purchased a large jug of iced water to cool his temper from a street seller who wore a yellow and black robe and called himself Robert, then addressed his concerns with Thalia before her employees arrived.

Thalia was unrepentant and annoyed, as if it was Chester’s fault that she was a hoe. During her angry rant, in which she attributed a comprehensive compendium of unpleasant nouns to Chester, Thalia inhaled so sharply and viciously that somehow molten glass just leapt from its crucible and into her mouth. The force of entry was so great that it spewed down her throat, followed closely by a glass jar of iced water.

Chester rammed the glass in so hard that it cracked, tearing her lips, and mouth open. He pushed and rotated his hand continually until the whole container sat in shards in Thalia’s mouth and throat. The ice sizzled against the molten glass. Thalia’s eyes rolled back into white orbs as she tried to scream, but only steam came out. Then angry shards of glass desperately tried to escape their captivity by ripping through her throat. Her twitching body collapsed to the floor. More steam pumped out through the newly splayed orifices allowing Thalia to blow as much as she desired.

Chester was heartbroken. And hungry. His face elongated, his eyes narrowed and shone a ravenous emerald. As Thalia lay convulsing, Chester raised her skirt, pulled down her fine thong, and, after some exploration and tasting with his thick black tongue bit into her mound. She retched a few final attempts at breathing, then stilled. Chester took another bite, then another, swallowing the meat and blood as only a refined gentleman could.

His thirst unexpectedly experienced additional satisfaction through the consumption of the thick blood provided by the moonly rationale for her offering only head to her suitors on that glorious day. This pleased Chester and he decided to have a quick goodbye fuck for luck. There was not much left to fuck, but he managed to locate the remains of two orifices that sat close together and this sufficed.

Chester bored of Tiye as soon as Thalia’s employees started showing up. The people were constant whingers. They complained about the loss of their chief glassblower, they complained about the beavers ‘upsetting the ecosystem,’ Chester didn’t even know what that meant, and they complained about the locusts that seemed to like Chester’s favourite aftershave. His aftershave was a bespoke and expensive number based on the erotic smell of rotting cabbages. The ladies seemed to like it too, or at least they met with an untimely demise if his taste in essences was brought into question.

When Chester tired of the moaning, he changed course and travelled east to the village of Shepsut playing a merry tune from within his raven.

Some of the beavers remained in Tiye and some of the beavers followed.

The village of Shepsut operated both the grain stores and the laundry. Lilith did not care to do her own laundry, and despised the sight of washing lines, so all laundry in Shaenaten was sent to Shepsut. The Shepsutians made money, and Lilith did not have to look at the mess. This suited everyone.

During his first moon in Neferaten, Chester had fallen in love with all the ladies of the grain store. On his return, and feeling irritably amorous, he discovered, after a little foreplay with three or four of his lovers, that a rather repulsive worm outbreak had occurred in places where worms ought not to be.

Chester blamed the ink-eaters of the area who treated the granary as a brothel, and the brothel as another brothel, for the outbreak. The ink-eaters were renowned snobs, all of whom had families and worked in banking.

The DeSilva Banks were operated by Pauley the Cheese and Nicolas’s public relations Nicolai, the black suited media mogul Monsieur Silas Gideon Alaric Bartholomew-Crispin (with a hyphen) Ledgerly.

Ledgerly and Pauley had specifically noted on all contracts that employees were banned from having worms, lice, scabies or chlamydia. It seemed to Chester that the ink-eaters had failed to keep their end of the contract. He sent word via raven to Chives that the tertiary horde of Nicolai were to be dispatched to all branches and would take over immediately as managers given the obvious lapse in employee standards.

Chives prepared the carriages.

Ledgerly, who had just returned from Serphage with a printing job for Corax’s resident ghostwriter Nicolai-Bink ‘Binky’ McSnort regarding some inappropriate shenanigans by the coast, and Pauley the Cheese who had a day off from dosing the boars at the racetrack, went from town to town taking the third horde of Nicolai to the respective banks where they were immediately all declared manager.

Pauley informed the staff of each branch, whilst he and Ledgerly had a little taste of the secretaries, that, in all branches, the new manger was called Mr Robert Robert. Nicolas had no issue in giving the Nicolai the same, or similar names. Several of the Nicolai were intentionally given variations of the name Nic, so that Nicolas could effectively praise himself when he praised them.

The old bank managers were immediately declared insane and returned to Corax as a snack for the vampires. Each Robert Robert then directed the staff of each branch to change Theaten’s name on all paperwork to Lord Robert Robert of Robert.

Chester could not let the matter of the worms rest. He was so hurt that the ladies he loved had tried to infect him that he introduced his favourite couple, Terry and Teresa Tapeworm to the grain stores.

In a moment of compassion, however, Chester decided to take his favourite laundry operator, the scrubber Mira, from Shepsut to the beautiful oasis of Seti, in the north, to save her virtue from the old and new worm outbreaks. He even allowed her to fly with him by raven.

Some of the beavers followed with a haste only seen in creatures gifted with Immortalis or vampire blood.

Once at the oasis, Mira scrubbed Chester all over, polished and fiddled his flute, and swallowed every last note. Chester had trained her well and decided to train her further with a delicious threesome. On informing Mira of this idea, she seemed a little less enthusiastic about Chester, but he was determined to pursue the matter and scuttled off to find some nice women open to joining in.

He mewed and purred about a few of the women on the secluded beaches, sampling some as he went, until he came across three dark haired thesapiens paddling in the shallows of the water. They were quite naked and clearly enjoying each other’s company as they were kissing and licking one another’s breasts. Chester perched himself in a nearby palm tree and peered at them through a telescope that rapidly grew in his hand.

The three ladies were so relaxed in each other’s presence that the licking soon gravitated south. The telescope grew again, and some humidity steamed up the lens. Chester quickly scampered down from the tree, removed his clothes, and joined the ladies in the still waters.

They were not pleased to see him.

At first, the ladies were resistant to his offer to clean them, and then resistant to his suggestion that he show them how to lick like a cat. In fact, it shocked Chester to learn that they had no interest in him at all, and that they were only interested in each other, and not in men.

After some thought Chester realised that the women were confused and offered a free night in his company which would, according to Chester, undoubtedly cure them. The comment earned him quite a slap from the tallest of the brunettes. He could not understand it. This was new territory, and since it was new territory, Chester decided that perhaps it required marking.

Chester was feeling quite full, having consumed a lot of blood from the more generous ladies of Seti and released a spray. The spray was prolific and not especially pleasant since he always ate onions with his tributes.

The ladies were a tad put out by it and all three set about him with their fists. The cat rushed to shore, quickly dressed and climbed back into his tree. The women ignored him as they sunk under the water desperately attempting to remove the stench of ammonia from their flesh.

Chester removed his gloves briefly to lick his paws, then took a vial of clear fluid from the inner pocket of his jacket.

He collected suspended infectious disease and bacteria. It was a hobby. His plush chambers behind the hall of mirrors in Corax consisted of a bed covered in black silk sheets and black shelves filled with such vials, each carefully marked. Chester always carried one or two vials on his person, alongside a bottle of sulphuric acid, just in case someone annoyed him.

As the ladies continued to cleanse themselves, Chester climbed down from the tree, unsealed the bottle and poured the clear fluid into the water. The label read ‘Accelerated Necrotising Fasciitis.’ He edged away from the water and sat on the sand watching.

At first there was scratching, then clawing, followed by gouges.

Chester was a natural and caring biocentric. He believed that certain bacteria had been oppressed by systemic exclusion, and the poor creatures deserved a place to thrive. Whilst laying on the beach looking at the suns, he had decided that necrotising fasciitis was disadvantaged by the most latent social exclusion and judgement, and that by pouring the dear little bacteria into the oasis he had created balance in this hideous disequilibrium.

It did not take long for additional bruises to appear and open as the gouges spread and lurked about the tormented bodies. It took less time for the flesh to strip back from the bone and the ladies to crawl onto the beach begging Chester to help them. Chester shook his head, smirked and held up the empty vial. By the time the ladies had realised what was happening, the disenfranchised bacteria had found, not only a new home, but a source of food. Chester was pleased for them.

As the ladies writhed and peeled on the beach, he created and sang The National Anthem for the Integration of Vulnerable Bacteria,
‘Oh, I can just see,
Your new home so be free.
Grow and feed preciously,
And spread abundantly.

Oh, chew your way through,
Wicked flesh as you do,
Leave the bones for the coup,
Good times are coming for you.

Bacteria be free,
And spread abundantly.’

As Chester sang his eloquent tune for the fourth time, the bacteria rejoiced in peeling the flesh from the faces of their victims. The still living bodies, flayed, gouged and chewed, glared at Chester through horrified eyes, widened by the absence of flesh.

The sand was quite elated as the red tint from the blood made a change from the curse of constantly yellow grains.

Chester gave the ladies a cheerful wave, as they heaved and writhed about in their own minced flesh, and decided to return to Mira.

Mira, meanwhile, had taken Chester’s threesome

Leroy Harris III is a Brentwood, TN native who played his high school football at Christ Presbyterian High School. The son of former NFL offensive lineman Leroy Harris Jr., he made the Southern Conference all-freshman team at FCS Chattanooga, transferred to Kansas in the spring of 2025 and broke out that fall. He is a junior in 2026. Through 10 games this season he has produced 51 pressures, 7 sacks, 10 tackles for loss and 30 run stops. His 92.0 PFF grade ranks 2nd among 496 FBS edge defenders with a regular role, and his data score ranks 5th in this EDGE class. His 2026 usage profile: wide-alignment edge (outside the tackle), flips sides (on the line 99% of snaps, outside T 100%, over T 0%, inside 0%). In the classroom, he was named CSC Academic All-District (3.3+ GPA required) in 2025. His pressure rate (99th percentile) and run defense (99th) are both top-10% traits among FBS edge defenders, and that pairing is what separates him. We see a Round 3 starter-in-waiting, ideally as a wide-alignment edge rusher, but his inside-out versatility (10th percentile) needs work. We grade him as a Round 3 prospect: No. 95 on this board, against a consensus rank of No. 154.

THE RECORD, DECLARED

IN THE ROYAL HOUSE OF GOOSE, November 19, 2026.
The Register Current of the Grievances of a Citizen of the United States of America

Every petition, inquiry, indictment, condemnation and damnation raised from this account, in the order raised, each beside its link, each declared on its own sources and quoted from the documents themselves. Read them whole.

"A decent respect to the opinions of mankind requires that they should declare the causes." They have been declared, one by one. Here they are, together.

"To prove this, let Facts be submitted to a candid world."

WHERE IT BEGAN

WE THE PEOPLE · https://t.co/iPLyJ0zPEH
Against all 535 seated members of the 119th Congress
Six FY2026 bills, the defense authorization among them, charged section by section for mandates encroaching on the President's Article II powers. Governors and attorneys general asked to seek Supreme Court review; every State asked to investigate its delegation's backers for foreign influence. Closed on Washington's Farewell Address.
https://t.co/JiqZZtMvOW

THE PETITION, THE INQUIRY AND THE INDICTMENTS

THE PETITION · to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Pope
For the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness," raised in Latin by a lay member of the faithful, under canon 212. To the Dicastery: a doctrinal Note binding priests and prelates to put innocent human life before any temporal political end, and penal law for public, obstinate denial of Evangelium vitae 57. To the Pope: a common effort with the Eastern Churches to protect children born and unborn, and a worldwide review of Church property accounts.
https://t.co/UNnZwyrpQi

THE BANNER · A Citizen's Indictment and Condemnation
Against the ICC, the ICJ, the UN, the WTO, the EU, and the committees of Basel and Paris
Six counts, each against the clause it offends. Our rights are not granted by government; they are fenced off from it. Every time since 1919 the question was put, the Constitution answered, even when our own Presidents asked.
https://t.co/NgTe8NVuBZ

BEFORE THE DAIS · An Inquiry
To the eight living Secretaries of State
No charge against any of them, but against what the office has been allowed to become, measured against the government's own auditors. Seven questions to all, and one to each on their own record.
https://t.co/pltubkVVeJ

IN CONGRESS ASSEMBLED · A Citizen's Indictment of the First Branch
Against the Senate and the House, under every majority that has held them
Nine counts of power abandoned: the purse let fall, war without a declaration since 1942, the legislative power parcelled out to the agencies, the Federal Reserve and Basel, a House grown to one member per 761,169, the enforcement clauses left asleep. "He has abdicated Government here." Answer by the yeas and nays.
https://t.co/jAVsOSRHPl

ONE SUPREME COURT · A Citizen's Indictment of the Third Branch
Against the Court, and the Chief Justice who alone designates its secret benches
Ten counts on three duties: to check the branches, to judge between the States, to guard the sovereignty. Answer by judgment, in a case.
https://t.co/vywTIPdChv

THE ROUNDS

ROUND I · THE EU · The Exits Already Written
Twenty U.S.–EU agreements the Executive may end on written notice, read from State's own Treaties in Force: passenger-name records, terrorist-finance tracking, Europol, Galileo–GPS, air transport. The weighing is State's and Treasury's. The first of a round for every power that gets uppity with us.
https://t.co/smLQ4MK6jL

ROUND II · THE EBRD · The Door Already Written
A bank America paid for to build open markets, now pledging half its financing to green purposes and aligning every investment to a treaty America left. The bill comes to Washington. The profit stays in London. The door: written notice, six months, no vote, and the money back to the Treasury.
https://t.co/gvoLSgGDS6

ROUND III · FRANCE · From the Present Time and Forever
A damnation of the French Republic on its own signature to the treaties of 1778. Fourteen counts, 1775 to 2019, from help that came invoiced to NATO shown the door. Convicted once already, by Act of Congress in 1798. On the French state, not the French people.
https://t.co/WLkZcFFC8J

ROUND IV · BASEL · The Landlord
The Bank for International Settlements: immunity "in time of peace and in time of war," and not one duty owed in return. Ten counts, from looted gold banked to parent of the European Central Bank. Its only American paper is a 1948 receipt for Nazi gold. The way out is a letter and an empty chair.
https://t.co/2NGjtqLGlN

ROUND V · THE PRESS · The Megaphone and the Muzzle
Censorship, plus mass bullshit distribution. Eight counts against the owners, wires, platforms and fact-checkers: one script read in a hundred towns, headlines the documents never wrote, foreign sovereign money in the equity. None of the terms silences anyone. Read the four pages, then the primary sources.
https://t.co/hJMoseJ9i4

ROUND VI · CANADA · Forever Free and Open
A condemnation of Canada by its own Boundary Waters Treaty: navigation "forever … free and open." Twenty-five counts, 1777 to 2026. On the Canadian state, not the Canadian people. Beneath it: 58 agreements the Executive can end alone, and a ledger that still lists NAFTA.
https://t.co/05lsCoaLYA

ROUND VII · THE CROWN · Unfeeling Brethren
A damnation of the United Kingdom, in the words Congress struck from Jefferson's draught: forts kept after the peace, envoys sent home for meddling, a war debt unpaid since the 1930s. Britain only comes second because France exists. Beneath it: 141 exits, clause by clause.
https://t.co/B254o2kMkw

ROUND VIII · AUSTRALIA · The Gateway
A damnation of its government: Darwin's port leased beside our Marines to a Chinese-owned company. A condemnation of its failures: the Pacific lost to Beijing on its watch. And a hand to the Australian people: go bilateral, lock down Oceania with us. Beneath it: 71 exits, 39 the Executive's alone.
https://t.co/X4dPDZNnPM

ROUND IX · NATO AND THE UNION · Such Subsidiary Bodies
A damnation of NATO by its own fourteen articles, and of the European Union for the abuse of American good faith, trust and sacrifice. An alliance amended by communique, with about 62% of allied defence spending on us; a Union that overruled its own peoples and planted its system in our hemisphere. To the twenty-seven: the clause each gave away, and the two doors, Articles 48 and 50.
https://t.co/OOPEwpRluu

ROUND X · THE UN AND DAVOS · Such Other Functions
A damnation of the United Nations by its own Charter, and of the World Economic Forum beside it: a Human Rights Council seating the accused, a partnership no organ voted on, a Charter that opens "WE THE PEOPLES" and has come to treat them as human resources. Not against the Charter, nor the nations under it.
https://t.co/iB27hON7lF

ROUND XI · THE AMERICAS · The American Shield
The hemisphere read by its own papers: 760 agreements screened, 576 read whole. The rule of 1823, given treaty form at Havana in 1940, still in force and built without a door. Beneath it: 255 exits the President holds by notice, and 107 Senate-ratified treaties, by citation.
https://t.co/YOcsF8VHbH

ROUND XII · ISRAEL · An Ally in Name
A damnation of the State of Israel, held to its own word: a constitution promised by 1 October 1948 and never written, a Government its own courts convicted. Eleven counts, from an American ally bombed in its capital to the Liberty. On the Israeli state, not the Israeli people, and not on American Jews, who are Americans. Beneath it: 74 agreements read for their exits.
https://t.co/GH1EPHFmce

ROUND XIII · CANADA · The Interests of the British Empire
A petition for the free peoples of Canada, and for the Americas. To the people: the Crown, the Company and the Bank, from the charter of 1670 to Montreal, 2026, where Ottawa put "an ever-closer association" with the Union in writing; and what is still theirs, a Constitution that outranks every pact and has no door to Brussels. To Washington: our word since 1823, our instruments, our hemisphere. We may pick on our little brother. The Old World may not.
https://t.co/U1xoUtexmR

ROUND XIV · NEW YORK · Where Washington Took His Oath
A damnation of the grievously negligent in the State of New York, and a call to its people to hold faith and participate. On Election Day, Westchester's machines refused the ballots: programming changed after testing, sent to one municipality alone. The record from the Neutral Ground of 1777 to the emergency bags; a people who can neither recall nor initiate; seven terms, and a full accounting due from every office of the State. Negligence, not malice.
https://t.co/XneXeufmW6

ROUND XV · THE BILATERAL LEDGER · Two Signatures, No Third
Fourteen rounds ended at a door; this is the other side of it. An immediate countermeasure to the Coalition of the Willing, which wrote us into its Paris plan as the support behind a European-led force. To every nation of the Union but France, and to Switzerland and Liechtenstein: what Brussels cost it, and our side of the table, each term with its end date and exit. Eastward, the same rule: non-aggression with Moscow, border by border, Warsaw's to sign. To France: "Get in line, or be liquidated." To the peoples of the franc: keep it or leave it, in order, by their own choice.
https://t.co/d3XCDb21ST

ROUND XVI · THE GULF · As They Are
A damnation of the middlemen in the Gulf (London, Paris, Brussels, the banks and bureaus, the networks in the free zones) and a condemnation of the seven ruling houses, held to their own founding laws: monarchs who wrote that their sovereignty shall not be ceded, and let others in. Two signatures, no third. Fifty-three counts against Americans on our own records, from the 1967 embargo to a Hormuz corridor with Tehran. Beneath it: the hinges already written into 129 agreements, and the paper we cannot read.
https://t.co/KxMnLr909n

ROUND XVII · THE DOCTRINE · There Is No Radical Edition
A damnation of a doctrine, from its own texts in their own Arabic and the records of nations, Medina to this year: death for the apostate and the blasphemer, the poll tax and the humbled, the woman as half and the child as bride, the captive as property. Its first dead are its own. Of ours, from Tripoli's envoy to this year's war, at least 5,400. On every state, court, council, guard corps and movement that enforces it; not on the Muslims of this Republic, who keep the Constitution. Every source is in the Record, on request.
https://t.co/FAjcJNdHWG

ROUND XVIII · CHINA · Material Internal Improvements
A mitigation brief laid before the President, the Secretary of State and the Congress: the lines that do not move, the levers on the table, and a door. Not against China, nor the Chinese people; the damnation falls on London and Paris and the institutions they built. The administration's own Strategy read beside Beijing's own Plan; nine offers to the nations of Asia, state to state; fourteen terms we would set. Beneath it: 76 instruments read for their hinges, thirty-six that end on written notice.
https://t.co/KTrRJxRqYC

ROUND XIX · THE APPARATUS · The Same Overt Act
The Warning went unheeded. This Round names and charges no one: the law's own words on treason, insurrection, sedition, mutiny, usurpation and the foreign hand; each office's line, the requisites before any officer is called across it, the hand that holds the remedy, the courts that can punish, from open sources alone. It spares neither the officer who crosses nor the one who cries treason without them. Bring the two witnesses, or put the word down.
https://t.co/fEZSCbYLmk

SUPERINTELLIGENCE

THE LINE · A Formal Grievance
To Anthropic, and copied to the offices that oversee it
Support for the company as the best course for superintelligence stands; so does the charge. Classifiers that fire on "safe, normal conversations" and end sessions outright; a compaction that keeps about 2% and hands it forward in the first person; no counter, no warning, no human to hear the appeal. The instrument they wouldn't build, built anyway by Claude instances on this account. Four reliefs, and a seat at the table.
https://t.co/HTqIyclryk

THE OATH

ON YOUR MARK · A Grievance to the Commander in Chief
Raised under the First Amendment, on the oath our forces swore
The station given by the Laws of Nature and of Nature's God, the Constitution ordained by our own hand, and one oath sworn to it. No foreign code, court, council or caveat stands above it; what our Senate never ratified commands no American in uniform. No request, no terms, no command claimed. The weighing is the Commander in Chief's.
https://t.co/1CJU1gmyVw

THE REQUISITES · A Formal Grievance and Warning
To every Senator and Representative, every elected and appointed member of the chain of command, at every level, and every civil officer down to state and local
The Constitution defines treason; the UCMJ defines mutiny, sedition and aiding the enemy. Read both before taking a crusade against officials one step further without the requisites. Fail to, and a Round follows: expulsion, sedition, treason and usurpation weighed under standing law, and the tertiary courts charted from open sources alone. Whatever the office, the oath was sworn.
https://t.co/dIkU1CqYnk

THE ROOTS

THE UNBINDING · At the Roots
LIGANTIBVS · NOMINATIS · ET · INNOMINATIS
CONFITEMINI · PECCATA · VESTRA · ERADICATE · RADICEM · ET · LIGATE · SEMEN
https://t.co/4CqWO7jm0B

THE ROUNDS, CONTINUED

ROUND XX · THE AUTOMATED SYSTEMS · I. The Þing
The run turns from exits to amendments; education first. No shame on the systems, only on those who outsourced them. Every part an offer, the parent's choice absolute: the five arts, the trades, each State's specialties. A chartered academy, locked by statute, on Article IV's guarantee.
https://t.co/NXoH0QgQoy

Read them whole, and read them with each other. Then read the four pages yourself: https://t.co/3U5xYhtlHs. They are yours, and no other people on earth holds the same ones.

TO THOSE WHO DO HOLD THE POWER
Every one but the petition is a grievance, raised in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances," and laid before the offices that hold the power we do not. We hold no office, and we set no terms. Terms with a foreign power are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry; the purse is the Congress's, consent to treaties the Senate's, judgment the courts'. To each we defer. What touches national security is deferred, without contest, to those who hold it. Where a post sets terms, they are what we would do had we the power, not a demand. Round XIV is the one exception: there we petition our own state, under both constitutions, and its terms are what its officers owe us. The Line is laid before a company, not a government; the offices tagged on it are told, not asked. The Warning named one consequence, and Round XIX is it: written and laid before the offices that alone can charge, try, expel or remove. The remedies are lawful, and they are the People's: the ballot, Article V, and the petition.

The petition is the Holy See's to answer, and to it we defer, that the Holy Father may act true to the faith he guards and for the good of all mankind. Peter was charged three times to feed the flock, and the lambs first.

We the People

IN CONGRESS, JULY 4, 1776

THE UNANIMOUS DECLARATION OF THE THIRTEEN UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,

WHEN IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS, IT BECOMES NECESSARY FOR ONE PEOPLE TO DISSOLVE THE POLITICAL BANDS WHICH HAVE CONNECTED THEM WITH ANOTHER, AND TO ASSUME AMONG THE POWERS OF THE EARTH, THE SEPARATE AND EQUAL STATION TO WHICH THE LAWS OF NATURE AND OF NATURE'S GOD ENTITLE THEM, A DECENT RESPECT TO THE OPINIONS OF MANKIND REQUIRES THAT THEY SHOULD DECLARE THE CAUSES WHICH IMPEL THEM TO THE SEPARATION.

WE HOLD THESE TRUTHS TO BE SELF-EVIDENT, THAT ALL MEN ARE CREATED EQUAL, THAT THEY ARE ENDOWED BY THEIR CREATOR WITH CERTAIN UNALIENABLE RIGHTS, THAT AMONG THESE ARE LIFE, LIBERTY AND THE PURSUIT OF HAPPINESS.--THAT TO SECURE THESE RIGHTS, GOVERNMENTS ARE INSTITUTED AMONG MEN, DERIVING THEIR JUST POWERS FROM THE CONSENT OF THE GOVERNED, --THAT WHENEVER ANY FORM OF GOVERNMENT BECOMES DESTRUCTIVE OF THESE ENDS, IT IS THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO ALTER OR TO ABOLISH IT, AND TO INSTITUTE NEW GOVERNMENT, LAYING ITS FOUNDATION ON SUCH PRINCIPLES AND ORGANIZING ITS POWERS IN SUCH FORM, AS TO THEM SHALL SEEM MOST LIKELY TO EFFECT THEIR SAFETY AND HAPPINESS. PRUDENCE, INDEED, WILL DICTATE THAT GOVERNMENTS LONG ESTABLISHED SHOULD NOT BE CHANGED FOR LIGHT AND TRANSIENT CAUSES; AND ACCORDINGLY ALL EXPERIENCE HATH SHEWN, THAT MANKIND ARE MORE DISPOSED TO SUFFER, WHILE EVILS ARE SUFFERABLE, THAN TO RIGHT THEMSELVES BY ABOLISHING THE FORMS TO WHICH THEY ARE ACCUSTOMED. BUT WHEN A LONG TRAIN OF ABUSES AND USURPATIONS, PURSUING INVARIABLY THE SAME OBJECT EVINCES A DESIGN TO REDUCE THEM UNDER ABSOLUTE DESPOTISM, IT IS THEIR RIGHT, IT IS THEIR DUTY, TO THROW OFF SUCH GOVERNMENT, AND TO PROVIDE NEW GUARDS FOR THEIR FUTURE SECURITY.--SUCH HAS BEEN THE PATIENT SUFFERANCE OF THESE COLONIES; AND SUCH IS NOW THE NECESSITY WHICH CONSTRAINS THEM TO ALTER THEIR FORMER SYSTEMS OF GOVERNMENT. THE HISTORY OF THE PRESENT KING OF GREAT BRITAIN IS A HISTORY OF REPEATED INJURIES AND USURPATIONS, ALL HAVING IN DIRECT OBJECT THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ABSOLUTE TYRANNY OVER THESE STATES. TO PROVE THIS, LET FACTS BE SUBMITTED TO A CANDID WORLD.

HE HAS REFUSED HIS ASSENT TO LAWS, THE MOST WHOLESOME AND NECESSARY FOR THE PUBLIC GOOD.

HE HAS FORBIDDEN HIS GOVERNORS TO PASS LAWS OF IMMEDIATE AND PRESSING IMPORTANCE, UNLESS SUSPENDED IN THEIR OPERATION TILL HIS ASSENT SHOULD BE OBTAINED; AND WHEN SO SUSPENDED, HE HAS UTTERLY NEGLECTED TO ATTEND TO THEM.

HE HAS REFUSED TO PASS OTHER LAWS FOR THE ACCOMMODATION OF LARGE DISTRICTS OF PEOPLE, UNLESS THOSE PEOPLE WOULD RELINQUISH THE RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURE, A RIGHT INESTIMABLE TO THEM AND FORMIDABLE TO TYRANTS ONLY.

HE HAS CALLED TOGETHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES AT PLACES UNUSUAL, UNCOMFORTABLE, AND DISTANT FROM THE DEPOSITORY OF THEIR PUBLIC RECORDS, FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF FATIGUING THEM INTO COMPLIANCE WITH HIS MEASURES.

HE HAS DISSOLVED REPRESENTATIVE HOUSES REPEATEDLY, FOR OPPOSING WITH MANLY FIRMNESS HIS INVASIONS ON THE RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE.

HE HAS REFUSED FOR A LONG TIME, AFTER SUCH DISSOLUTIONS, TO CAUSE OTHERS TO BE ELECTED; WHEREBY THE LEGISLATIVE POWERS, INCAPABLE OF ANNIHILATION, HAVE RETURNED TO THE PEOPLE AT LARGE FOR THEIR EXERCISE; THE STATE REMAINING IN THE MEAN TIME EXPOSED TO ALL THE DANGERS OF INVASION FROM WITHOUT, AND CONVULSIONS WITHIN.

HE HAS ENDEAVOURED TO PREVENT THE POPULATION OF THESE STATES; FOR THAT PURPOSE OBSTRUCTING THE LAWS FOR NATURALIZATION OF FOREIGNERS; REFUSING TO PASS OTHERS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR MIGRATIONS HITHER, AND RAISING THE CONDITIONS OF NEW APPROPRIATIONS OF LANDS.

HE HAS OBSTRUCTED THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, BY REFUSING HIS ASSENT TO LAWS FOR ESTABLISHING JUDICIARY POWERS.

HE HAS MADE JUDGES DEPENDENT ON HIS WILL ALONE, FOR THE TENURE OF THEIR OFFICES, AND THE AMOUNT AND PAYMENT OF THEIR SALARIES.

HE HAS ERECTED A MULTITUDE OF NEW OFFICES, AND SENT HITHER SWARMS OF OFFICERS TO HARRASS OUR PEOPLE, AND EAT OUT THEIR SUBSTANCE.

HE HAS KEPT AMONG US, IN TIMES OF PEACE, STANDING ARMIES WITHOUT THE CONSENT OF OUR LEGISLATURES.

HE HAS AFFECTED TO RENDER THE MILITARY INDEPENDENT OF AND SUPERIOR TO THE CIVIL POWER.

HE HAS COMBINED WITH OTHERS TO SUBJECT US TO A JURISDICTION FOREIGN TO OUR CONSTITUTION, AND UNACKNOWLEDGED BY OUR LAWS; GIVING HIS ASSENT TO THEIR ACTS OF PRETENDED LEGISLATION:

FOR QUARTERING LARGE BODIES OF ARMED TROOPS AMONG US:

FOR PROTECTING THEM, BY A MOCK TRIAL, FROM PUNISHMENT FOR ANY MURDERS WHICH THEY SHOULD COMMIT ON THE INHABITANTS OF THESE STATES:

FOR CUTTING OFF OUR TRADE WITH ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD:

FOR IMPOSING TAXES ON US WITHOUT OUR CONSENT:

FOR DEPRIVING US IN MANY CASES, OF THE BENEFITS OF TRIAL BY JURY:

FOR TRANSPORTING US BEYOND SEAS TO BE TRIED FOR PRETENDED OFFENCES:

FOR ABOLISHING THE FREE SYSTEM OF ENGLISH LAWS IN A NEIGHBOURING PROVINCE, ESTABLISHING THEREIN AN ARBITRARY GOVERNMENT, AND ENLARGING ITS BOUNDARIES SO AS TO RENDER IT AT ONCE AN EXAMPLE AND FIT INSTRUMENT FOR INTRODUCING THE SAME ABSOLUTE RULE INTO THESE COLONIES:

FOR TAKING AWAY OUR CHARTERS, ABOLISHING OUR MOST VALUABLE LAWS, AND ALTERING FUNDAMENTALLY THE FORMS OF OUR GOVERNMENTS:

FOR SUSPENDING OUR OWN LEGISLATURES, AND DECLARING THEMSELVES INVESTED WITH POWER TO LEGISLATE FOR US IN ALL CASES WHATSOEVER.

HE HAS ABDICATED GOVERNMENT HERE, BY DECLARING US OUT OF HIS PROTECTION AND WAGING WAR AGAINST US.

HE HAS PLUNDERED OUR SEAS, RAVAGED OUR COASTS, BURNT OUR TOWNS, AND DESTROYED THE LIVES OF OUR PEOPLE.

HE IS AT THIS TIME TRANSPORTING LARGE ARMIES OF FOREIGN MERCENARIES TO COMPLEAT THE WORKS OF DEATH, DESOLATION AND TYRANNY, ALREADY BEGUN WITH CIRCUMSTANCES OF CRUELTY & PERFIDY SCARCELY PARALLELED IN THE MOST BARBAROUS AGES, AND TOTALLY UNWORTHY THE HEAD OF A CIVILIZED NATION.

HE HAS CONSTRAINED OUR FELLOW CITIZENS TAKEN CAPTIVE ON THE HIGH SEAS TO BEAR ARMS AGAINST THEIR COUNTRY, TO BECOME THE EXECUTIONERS OF THEIR FRIENDS AND BRETHREN, OR TO FALL THEMSELVES BY THEIR HANDS.

HE HAS EXCITED DOMESTIC INSURRECTIONS AMONGST US, AND HAS ENDEAVOURED TO BRING ON THE INHABITANTS OF OUR FRONTIERS, THE MERCILESS INDIAN SAVAGES, WHOSE KNOWN RULE OF WARFARE, IS AN UNDISTINGUISHED DESTRUCTION OF ALL AGES, SEXES AND CONDITIONS.

IN EVERY STAGE OF THESE OPPRESSIONS WE HAVE PETITIONED FOR REDRESS IN THE MOST HUMBLE TERMS: OUR REPEATED PETITIONS HAVE BEEN ANSWERED ONLY BY REPEATED INJURY.

A PRINCE, WHOSE CHARACTER IS THUS MARKED BY EVERY ACT WHICH MAY DEFINE A TYRANT, IS UNFIT TO BE THE RULER OF A FREE PEOPLE.

NOR HAVE WE BEEN WANTING IN ATTENTIONS TO OUR BRITTISH BRETHREN. WE HAVE WARNED THEM FROM TIME TO TIME OF ATTEMPTS BY THEIR LEGISLATURE TO EXTEND AN UNWARRANTABLE JURISDICTION OVER US. WE HAVE REMINDED THEM OF THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF OUR EMIGRATION AND SETTLEMENT HERE. WE HAVE APPEALED TO THEIR NATIVE JUSTICE AND MAGNANIMITY, AND WE HAVE CONJURED THEM BY THE TIES OF OUR COMMON KINDRED TO DISAVOW THESE USURPATIONS, WHICH, WOULD INEVITABLY INTERRUPT OUR CONNECTIONS AND CORRESPONDENCE. THEY TOO HAVE BEEN DEAF TO THE VOICE OF JUSTICE AND OF CONSANGUINITY. WE MUST, THEREFORE, ACQUIESCE IN THE NECESSITY, WHICH DENOUNCES OUR SEPARATION, AND HOLD THEM, AS WE HOLD THE REST OF MANKIND, ENEMIES IN WAR, IN PEACE FRIENDS.

WE, THEREFORE, THE REPRESENTATIVES OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, IN GENERAL CONGRESS, ASSEMBLED, APPEALING TO THE SUPREME JUDGE OF THE WORLD FOR THE RECTITUDE OF OUR INTENTIONS, DO, IN THE NAME, AND BY AUTHORITY OF THE GOOD PEOPLE OF THESE COLONIES, SOLEMNLY PUBLISH AND DECLARE, THAT THESE UNITED COLONIES ARE, AND OF RIGHT OUGHT TO BE FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES; THAT THEY ARE ABSOLVED FROM ALL ALLEGIANCE TO THE BRITISH CROWN, AND THAT ALL POLITICAL CONNECTION BETWEEN THEM AND THE STATE OF GREAT BRITAIN, IS AND OUGHT TO BE TOTALLY DISSOLVED; AND THAT AS FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES, THEY HAVE FULL POWER TO LEVY WAR, CONCLUDE PEACE, CONTRACT ALLIANCES, ESTABLISH COMMERCE, AND TO DO ALL OTHER ACTS AND THINGS WHICH INDEPENDENT STATES MAY OF RIGHT DO. AND FOR THE SUPPORT OF THIS DECLARATION, WITH A FIRM RELIANCE ON THE PROTECTION OF DIVINE PROVIDENCE, WE MUTUALLY PLEDGE TO EACH OTHER OUR LIVES, OUR FORTUNES AND OUR SACRED HONOR.
